awd_titl_txt: Travel: 2025 International Programming Language Implementation Summer School (PLISS)
awd_abstract_narration:
This award provides student travel and subsistence for the 2025 International Programming Language Implementation Summer School (PLISS) to be held May 26 -- May 31, 2025, in Bertinoro, Italy. This summer school provides an important and valuable educational opportunity for students to study topics related to designs and implementations of programming languages. The award's broader significance and importance include building international community and enhancing education of US students, including students from historically underrepresented groups. The school also provides students exposure to and multiple opportunities to interact with leading-edge research and researchers. By supporting US-based students, the school thus imparts training to the next generation of researchers in design and implementation of programming languages in both industry and academia, as well as to future application developers.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The Sixth International Programming Language Implementation Summer School (PLISS'25) was held May 26-31, 2025, in Bertinoro, Italy, bringing together 45 students from diverse backgrounds with nine world-class researchers in programming language design and implementation. Organized by Prof. Jan Vitek (Northeastern University) and Prof. Laurence Tratt (King's College London), the school achieved its mission of preparing early-career researchers for advanced study in the field.

 The school featured an exceptional lineup of speakers from leading academic institutions and industry. Topics spanned the breadth of modern programming language implementation, including Ranjit Jhala (UC San Diego) on refinement types for Rust, Shriram Krishnamurthi (Brown University) on human factors in formal methods, and David Chisnall (Cambridge/SCI Semiconductor) on hardware-software co-design with CHERI systems. Additional lectures covered OCaml optimization and memory analysis by Nick Benton (Cambridge) and Greta Yorsh (Jane Street), runtime security by Jeremy Singer (Glasgow), WebAssembly engine design by Ben Titzer (Carnegie Mellon), program synthesis by Hila Peleg (Technion), and programming systems theory by Tomas Petricek (Charles University).   With support from an NSF travel grant,  US students attended the school, selected with priority given to students of a variety of backgrounds and students from less-funded institutions. The intimate 45-participant setting fostered meaningful interactions between students and faculty, creating opportunities for in-depth technical discussions and mentoring.

PLISS'25 strengthened connections between US and international researchers, inspired students to pursue careers in programming languages research, and contributed to building a more diverse and vibrant research community in this area of computer science.
